comment: The states a reader can put the viewer in, rather than a list of pages: a
flipbook is one page whose accessibility changes as it is used. Each state
names the demo settings it needs and the steps that reach it.
The demo is built and served from demo-dist by the scanner, so a run needs
nothing else running and works the same in CI as it does here.

states.comment: The book as a page first shows it.
After a page turn: a different spread, and a rendered canvas.
One page at a time, the layout a phone gets.
Right to left, where the controls keep their meaning but swap sides.
The book over the page: a dialog, and the hardest state to get right.
Filling the screen. The click is a real one, so the browser allows it.
After the share button reports back, since it adds a live region.
